title: Lighting Layout — the lumen method on a room, and the grid it asks for
description:
A parametric LIGHTING LAYOUT on the six-node spine — Geometry → Input Properties → Math Engine → Output Metrics → 2D Render + 3D Render.

DROP IT ON A SPACE. It reads the room polygon and answers the one question a general lighting layer asks: how many, and where.

THE AREA IS THE SHOELACE ON THE OUTLINE, not the bounding box. An L-shaped room is not a rectangle and the lumen method divides by the area, so using the box would over-light every room that is not one.

THE LUMEN METHOD IS ONE LINE. `N = (E × A) / (F × UF × MF)` — the light you need over the light one fitting delivers, rounded up to a whole fixture. Everything above it is the inputs and everything below it is where they go.

THE UTILISATION FACTOR IS A PROP, NOT A GUESS. A real UF comes off the manufacturer's table against the room index and the three reflectances. `roomIndex` is computed so you can read that table, and `suggestedUF` is a documented fit — calibrated so a room index of 1.0 with 70/50/20 reflectances lands near 0.52, which is where a manufacturer’s table puts a recessed downlight — reported BESIDE the one you typed rather than instead of it — a number this object invented has no business silently deciding how many fittings a room gets.

IT WILL ALMOST ALWAYS OVERSHOOT. The count is rounded up to a whole fixture and then up again to fill a rectangle, so a room that needs 4.2 fittings gets 6. `overshoot` says by how much, because that is the number you dim against later.

SPACING IS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED. `spacingOk` compares the grid pitch against the spacing-to-height rule — a grid that satisfies the lumen method and violates the spacing rule is bright and blotchy, and the two are separate failures.

DIMENSIONS AT THE DEFAULTS: a 14.79 m² room, RI 0.99, 200 lx target, 650 lm fittings at UF 0.50 and MF 0.8 — 12 required, laid out 4 × 3 inside a 0.6 m setback, achieving 211 lx: a 5.4 % overshoot. The suggested UF comes back 0.52 against the 0.50 typed.

WHAT THIS CANNOT DO. No point-by-point calculation, no obstructions, no daylight contribution. Grid and staggered only — a perimeter or feature layout is placed by hand.

props.name: Material
props.value: as the chosen downlight — this object places, it does not detail

props.name: Semantics
props.value: evenly lit room, general ambient layer, no drama

params.name: Lighting Layout maths
params.expr:
_natL = max(0.5, _hostL)
# Host frame — node, segment or space
_e1 = hcat(1, 0)
_np = rows(P)
_isSeg = _np == 2
_isSpace = _np > 2
_edges = _isSpace ? (shift(P, -1) - P) : _e1
_edgeLen = len(_edges)
_longest = max(_edgeLen)
_spaceDir = _isSpace ? row(compress(_edges, eq(_edgeLen, _longest)), 0) : _e1
_segDir = _isSeg ? (row(P, 1) - row(P, 0)) : _e1
_dir = _isSpace ? _spaceDir : (_isSeg ? _segDir : _e1)
_dirLen = len(_dir)
_axisB = _dirLen > 0 ? normalize(_dir) : _e1
_rot = rotation * PI / 180
_crot = cos(_rot)
_srot = sin(_rot)
_bx = sub(_axisB, 0, 0, 1, 1)
_by = sub(_axisB, 0, 1, 1, 1)
_axisU = hcat(_bx * _crot - _by * _srot, _bx * _srot + _by * _crot)
_axisV = (flipSide > 0 ? -1 : 1) * perp(_axisU)
_ux = sub(_axisU, 0, 0, 1, 1)
_uy = sub(_axisU, 0, 1, 1, 1)
_vx = sub(_axisV, 0, 0, 1, 1)
_vy = sub(_axisV, 0, 1, 1, 1)
_Qu = col(P, 0) * _ux + col(P, 1) * _uy
_Qv = col(P, 0) * _vx + col(P, 1) * _vy
_hu0 = _np > 0 ? min(_Qu) : 0
_hu1 = _np > 0 ? max(_Qu) : 0
_hv0 = _np > 0 ? min(_Qv) : 0
_hv1 = _np > 0 ? max(_Qv) : 0
_hcu = (_hu0 + _hu1) / 2
_hcv = (_hv0 + _hv1) / 2
_hostL = _hu1 - _hu0
_hostW = _hv1 - _hv0
# Fit to host — one uniform scale, Max never enlarges
_availL = max(0, _hostL - 2 * margin)
_notOff = fitMode != 'Off'
_exact = fitMode == 'Exact'
_sRaw = _natL > 0 ? _availL / _natL : 1
_sFit = (_notOff && _availL > 0) ? (_exact ? _sRaw : min(1, _sRaw)) : 1
scale = max(0.15, min(5, _sFit))
_s = scale
_bodyL = _hostL
_bodyW = _hostW
# Anchor — place the footprint by any of the nine box points
_anchorL = anchorDir == 'Top-Left' || anchorDir == 'Left-Center' || anchorDir == 'Bottom-Left'
_anchorR = anchorDir == 'Top-Right' || anchorDir == 'Right-Center' || anchorDir == 'Bottom-Right'
_anchorT = anchorDir == 'Top-Left' || anchorDir == 'Top-Center' || anchorDir == 'Top-Right'
_anchorB = anchorDir == 'Bottom-Left' || anchorDir == 'Bottom-Center' || anchorDir == 'Bottom-Right'
_ax = _anchorR - _anchorL
_ay = _anchorB - _anchorT
_hau = _hcu + _ax * max(0, _hostL / 2 - margin)
_hav = _hcv + _ay * max(0, _hostW / 2 - margin)
_cu = _hau - _ax * _bodyL / 2
_cv = _hav - _ay * _bodyW / 2
_wcx = _cu * _ux + _cv * _vx
_wcy = _cu * _uy + _cv * _vy
# The room's real area, by the shoelace on its own outline — not the bounding box, because an
# L-shaped room is not a rectangle and the lumen method divides by the area.
_px = col(P, 0)
_py = col(P, 1)
_pxn = shift(_px, -1)
_pyn = shift(_py, -1)
_shoe = rows(P) > 2 ? sum(_px * _pyn - _pxn * _py) : 0
roomArea = abs(_shoe) / 2
_A = max(0.5, roomArea)
# Room index — the shape of the room as one number. A tall narrow room wastes light on its
# walls and a low wide one does not, and this is the axis every utilisation table is read on.
_Hm = max(0.3, mountHeight - workPlane)
_rl = max(0.5, _hostL)
_rw = max(0.5, _hostW)
roomIndex = (_rl * _rw) / (_Hm * (_rl + _rw))
# A suggestion, not an answer. A real utilisation factor comes off the manufacturer's table
# against the room index and the three reflectances; this is a documented fit to sanity-check
# the number that was typed, and it is reported beside it rather than instead of it.
suggestedUF = max(0.2, min(0.85, 1.071 * (roomIndex / (roomIndex + 0.63)) * (0.6 + 0.4 * reflCeiling) * (0.85 + 0.15 * reflWall) * (0.95 + 0.1 * reflFloor)))
_uf = max(0.1, utilisationFactor)
_mf = max(0.4, maintenanceFactor)
# The lumen method, and it is one line: the light you need over the light one fitting delivers.
requiredFixtures = ceil((targetLux * _A) / max(1, fixtureLumens * _uf * _mf))
# Lay that many out on the closest thing to a square grid the room's proportions allow.
_gL = max(0.3, _rl - 2 * edgeSetback)
_gW = max(0.3, _rw - 2 * edgeSetback)
_nx = max(1, round(sqrt(max(1, requiredFixtures) * _gL / _gW)))
_ny = max(1, ceil(max(1, requiredFixtures) / _nx))
_pu = _gL / _nx
_pv = _gW / _ny
_nG = _nx * _ny
_k = arange(_nG)
_iy = floor(_k / _nx)
_ix = _k - _iy * _nx
# A staggered layout offsets every other row by half a pitch. There is no modulo here, so the
# parity is `row - 2 * floor(row / 2)`, which is the same thing written with what exists.
_odd = _iy - 2 * floor(_iy / 2)
_stag = arrangement == 'Staggered' ? (_odd * _pu / 2) : (_odd * 0)
_gu = 0 - _gL / 2 + (_ix + 0.5) * _pu + _stag
_gv = 0 - _gW / 2 + (_iy + 0.5) * _pv
_mr = markerRadius * _s
_mz = mountHeight * _s
_oneG = ones(_nG, 1)
_MARK = hcat(_gu - _mr, _gv - _mr, _gu + _mr, _gv - _mr, _gu + _mr, _gv + _mr, _gu - _mr, _gv + _mr, (_mz - 0.02) * _oneG, _mz * _oneG, 1 * _oneG)
_GRID = hcat(0 - _gL / 2, 0 - _gW / 2, _gL / 2, 0 - _gW / 2, _gL / 2, _gW / 2, 0 - _gL / 2, _gW / 2, _mz - 0.001, _mz, 2)
Q = vcat(_MARK, _GRID)
# Quad prism — every part is a quad swept from z0 to z1 (6 faces)
_nq = rows(Q)
_r4 = ones(4,1)
_a1 = col(Q,0)
_b1 = col(Q,1)
_a2 = col(Q,2)
_b2 = col(Q,3)
_a3 = col(Q,4)
_b3 = col(Q,5)
_a4 = col(Q,6)
_b4 = col(Q,7)
_qz0 = col(Q,8)
_qz1 = col(Q,9)
_gq = kron(col(Q,10), _r4)
_fq = kron(arange(_nq), _r4) * 6
_q0 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a1,_b1,_qz0,_a2,_b2,_qz0,_a3,_b3,_qz0,_a4,_b4,_qz0), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 0, _gq)
_q1 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a1,_b1,_qz1,_a2,_b2,_qz1,_a3,_b3,_qz1,_a4,_b4,_qz1), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 1, _gq)
_q2 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a1,_b1,_qz0,_a2,_b2,_qz0,_a2,_b2,_qz1,_a1,_b1,_qz1), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 2, _gq)
_q3 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a2,_b2,_qz0,_a3,_b3,_qz0,_a3,_b3,_qz1,_a2,_b2,_qz1), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 3, _gq)
_q4 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a3,_b3,_qz0,_a4,_b4,_qz0,_a4,_b4,_qz1,_a3,_b3,_qz1), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 4, _gq)
_q5 = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a4,_b4,_qz0,_a1,_b1,_qz0,_a1,_b1,_qz1,_a4,_b4,_qz1), 4*_nq, 3), _fq + 5, _gq)
_FL = vcat(_q0,_q1,_q2,_q3,_q4,_q5)
_PL = hcat(reshape(hcat(_a1,_b1,_a2,_b2,_a3,_b3,_a4,_b4), 4*_nq, 2), kron(arange(_nq), _r4), _gq)
# Local (u,v,z) -> world, once, for every part at the same time
_U = _cu + col(_FL,0)
_V = _cv + col(_FL,1)
_W = hcat(_U * _ux + _V * _vx, _U * _uy + _V * _vy, col(_FL,2), col(_FL,3), col(_FL,4))
_nw = rows(_W)
_PU = _cu + col(_PL,0)
_PV = _cv + col(_PL,1)
_WP = hcat(_PU * _ux + _PV * _vx, _PU * _uy + _PV * _vy, col(_PL,2), col(_PL,3))
_nwp = rows(_WP)
Markers3D = sub(compress(_W, eq(col(_W,4), 1)), 0, 0, _nw, 4)
GridPlan = sub(compress(_WP, eq(col(_WP,3), 2)), 0, 0, _nwp, 3)
_gwx = (_cu + _gu) * _ux + (_cv + _gv) * _vx
_gwy = (_cu + _gu) * _uy + (_cv + _gv) * _vy
MarkerPlan = hcat(_gwx, _gwy, _mr * _oneG)
# ── Lamp block ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The photometry a renderer needs and a drawing cannot show. Arithmetic on the inputs only:
# nothing here lights anything, and `lamp` names the Photometry file that carries the rest.
_lbDim = max(0, min(100, dimLevel)) / 100
_lbLm = fixtureLumens * _nG
lampDimmed = _lbLm * _lbDim
# 683 lm/W is the same constant material/1 uses for emission.luminance. Writing it in both
# places is the point: a lit diffuser and the lamp behind it have to be reconcilable, and they
# can only be reconciled through one number.
lampWatts = lampDimmed / 683
lampSoftSize = lampRadius
lampEmits = emitsLight > 0 ? 1 : 0
lampCri = cri
lampKelvin = kelvin
# What the grid actually delivers, which is not what was asked for: the count was rounded up to
# a whole fixture and then up again to fill a rectangle, so the room is almost always brighter
# than the target. Saying by how much is the point.
achievedLux = (_nG * fixtureLumens * _uf * _mf * (max(0, min(100, dimLevel)) / 100)) / _A
gridX = _nx
gridY = _ny
gridTotal = _nG
pitchU = _pu
pitchV = _pv
maxSpacing = spacingRatio * _Hm
spacingOk = (max(_pu, _pv) <= spacingRatio * _Hm) ? 1 : 0
mountingHeightAbovePlane = _Hm
utilisationUsed = _uf
overshoot = targetLux > 0 ? (100 * (achievedLux - targetLux) / targetLux) : 0
arrangementCode = arrangement == 'Grid' ? 0 : 1
